newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada investigating steel plate dumping charges.
newsitem.headline: Canada investigating steel plate dumping charges.

text.p: The Canadian government said on Thursday it was investigating the alleged dumping of hot-rolled carbon steel plate by a number of offshore producers.
The federal agency Revenue Canada said the alleged dumping was from China, Russia, Mexico, Poland and South Africa and Russia.

A statement said it began its investigation after a complaint from Stelco Inc alleging that dumping was harming Canadian producers by eroding and suppressing prices, reducing sales and profitability and stopping producers from working at full capacity.

The material is most commonly used to produce rail cars, oil- and gas-storage tanks, heavy construction machinery, agricultural equipment and parts for cars and trucks. It is also used to build bridges, factories, office towers, ships and pressure vessels.
Dumping happens when goods are sold to importers in Canada at a loss or at prices that are less than selling prices at home.
Revenue Canada expects to reach a preliminary decision in 90 days.
